programs.title: Bridges of Work: From Roman Builders to Agent-Managed Workplaces
outcomes: Explain how an aqueduct bridge like the Pont du Gard was engineered and maintained by organized labor over two millennia
Analyze how agent-managed DAO structures change task routing and working-group coordination
Draft worker input questions for governance decisions where humans hold final votes

sessions.activity: Study the DAO charter and contribution model; compare Roman-era public works governance with the mission of governing AI as a public good.
Use Evidence Monitor outputs on automation and work; practice summarizing evidence for bargaining positions.
Simulate a working group: Task Router assigns tasks, participants negotiate roles and escalation paths.
Draft a workplace proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter agent, then hold a human-only vote to enact or reject it.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized session feedback and task-routing simulation outcomes; no personal or workplace-identifying data contributed.
programs.consent: Voluntary enrollment with signed informed consent; participants may opt out of any data contribution; workplace identifiers never collected.

programs.title: Aqueduct Engineers: Water, Stone and Shared Decisions
outcomes: Describe how the Pont du Gard carried water across the Gardon gorge and why it still stands
Identify local map features (river, scrub, woodland, quarries) from the world map
Explain why some decisions in a DAO are reserved for humans

sessions.activity: Explore the world map of the Pont du Gard area: count bridges, woods and the river; learn how the Roman quarry at L'Estel supplied stone.
Read a kid-friendly charter; discuss what 'public good' means and list outcomes the class wants to measure.
In teams, draft a class proposal for a bridge-themed project; the class votes, with only students casting the final vote.
Track progress on the class charter outcomes using simple charts updated each week.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, aggregated quiz scores and project rubric results; no individual names or personal details shared.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent required for participation and any data contribution; guardians may withdraw consent at any time; no identifiable student data leaves the classroom.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: Mission-Driven DAO Literacy
outcomes: Map an NGO mission onto a DAO charter with measurable outcomes
Use agent-generated evidence summaries responsibly in advocacy
Design a proposal workflow that keeps enactment decisions with people

sessions.activity: Workshop: translate an NGO mission statement into charter outcomes and a contribution model, using the world's charter as template.
Evaluate Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent outputs for bias, gaps and citation quality.
Draft a real funding proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; peer-review which enactment steps stay human-reserved.
Build a progress dashboard aligned to charter outcomes; define what success looks like in 6 months.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal drafts and evaluation rubrics to a shared model of agent-drafting quality; organization names stripped.
programs.consent: Organizational consent via MOU plus individual opt-in; data minimized and anonymized before sharing; withdrawal permitted at any time.

programs.title: Shared Water, Shared Governance: Nonprofit Programs in an Agent-Managed World
outcomes: Understand the division of labor between agents (operate) and humans (govern) in resource-allocation decisions
Connect local heritage stewardship, like the Pont du Gard landscape, to long-term public-goods thinking
Run a mock decision cycle from evidence to human vote

sessions.activity: Tour the five zones conceptually; discuss why treasury transfers and charter amendments are human-reserved.
Case study: evidence synthesis on a shared resource (the Gardon River), comparing agent summaries with human field knowledge.
Collaborator Scout exercise: identify stakeholder roles for a river-heritage program; Task Router simulation assigns working-group tasks.
Small groups draft a community program proposal; a volunteer steward panel holds the final vote.
Set measurable outcomes and a simple tracking cadence for the mock program.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program-design templates and voting simulation results; no beneficiary or donor data shared.
programs.consent: Layered consent: board approval for program data, individual opt-in for participation records; privacy policy shared up front; opt-out honored immediately.
